newsitem.title: MEXICO: Metallica Resources to pour Mexican gold in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Metallica Resources to pour Mexican gold in 1998.

text.p: - Toronto-based Metallica Resources Inc will start up a new Mexican gold-silver mine in 1998 and will be producing the precious metals that year, the company president said here Tuesday.

Louis A. Lepry told the Mexico Mining 1997 conference here that plant construction work was scheduled to start at the company's Cerro San Pedro gold project in San Luis Potosi state in August this year and end in January 1998, with output expected between March and June next year.

"We will be pouring some gold in 1998," Lepry said, adding the company objective was to reach annual gold output levels of 150,000 ounces and a silver production of 4 million ounces per year using open pit mining and leach pad methods.

Lepry said feasibility study working parameters concluded the 400 hectare property had reserves (proven and probable reserves above incremental cutoffs) of 77.3 million tonnes at 0.6 gramme/tonne gold and 24.8 grammes/tonne silver, which he said worked out to 1.5 million ounces of gold and 62 million ounces of silver.
Lepry said capital costs of the low-grade mine start up would total around $75 million and he anticipated total operational costs of $230 per ounce of gold.
Cerro San Pedro, which has been producing dating back to 1570, has in the past 400 years produced around 2.5 million ounces of gold and between 40 to 50 million ounces of silver, Lepry said.
